active_paradigms.idea: Replace the source-global fixed-charge MILP with a partition-aware capacitated directed-Steiner MILP using scipy.optimize.milp
active_paradigms.description: The current program is an exact-looking directed Steiner formulation: a binary edge activation variable is paid once and one continuous source-to-terminal commodity is constrained by that activation. Its major strength is that it captures shared multicast prefixes across destinations and therefore can beat independent shortest paths. However, it activates an edge once for all partitions, sends every partition on exactly the same recovered tree, and entirely ignores the throughput field, so it can receive an unrealistically cheap objective or produce a topology that cannot exploit or satisfy parallel-network constraints. Build deterministic variables x[p,e] for whether partition p is transmitted over edge e and f[p,t,e] for whether that partition reaches terminal t through e. Charge cost[e]/num_partitions for each x[p,e] if partitions are equal data slices, while allowing f[p,t,e] <= x[p,e] so destinations still share a transmission of the same partition. Add edge-capacity constraints based on the evaluator's expected per-partition transfer rate, such as sum_p rate[p]*x[p,e] <= throughput[e], or use per-edge partition-count limits if the evaluator treats each path as one flow. Solve this single global MILP with scipy.optimize.milp and recover each destination/partition path from the selected arcs, removing cycles before writing paths. This retains the proven broadcast-sharing principle while making the decision variables match the actual output structure and enabling different partitions to use distinct parallel routes when capacity makes that beneficial.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary transfer-cost score through valid sharing within each partition, plus throughput-feasible parallel routing and avoidance of falsely sharing an edge across different partitions.
active_paradigms.cautions: The supplied wrapper exposes no actual scoring logic, so verify whether an edge is charged once per partition, once per destination path, or once globally before choosing the x-variable indexing and cost coefficient. Do not use unpriced edges as unit-cost arcs. A pure directed-Steiner model without explicit rates should not invent throughput constraints unless evaluator validation actually checks them; otherwise retain the partition-aware sharing model but omit those constraints. Require an incumbent with every (partition,destination) reachable before accepting a time-limited result.

active_paradigms.idea: Use a capacitated per-copy transfer model solved directly by networkx.network_simplex when the evaluator charges every destination-path transmission
active_paradigms.description: This is a deliberately different model for the plausible evaluator interpretation in which each returned destination/partition path pays for every traversal rather than receiving fixed-charge multicast discounts. Construct a demand network with one unit, or the appropriate fractional data amount, demanded by every destination-partition pair and capacities derived from edge throughput. Assign each edge its monetary cost per transferred unit and use node demands so the source supplies total demand while destination-partition sink copies consume their required units. Call networkx.network_simplex once to obtain the globally minimum-cost feasible integral min-cost flow instead of independently calling shortest path for each receiver. Decompose the resulting positive flows into source-to-destination paths and write these into BroadCastTopology. Unlike the current MILP, this model naturally prices congestion and can split aggregate demand over several inexpensive networks where doing so is cheaper or necessary. It is especially promising if the low current score is constrained by path-level accounting rather than by a true fixed-charge broadcast evaluator. It also has much lower formulation overhead than a commodity-per-terminal MILP on larger hidden instances.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Total path-transmission cost under throughput capacities, load balancing across links, and deterministic feasibility when each partition or destination is independently billed.
active_paradigms.cautions: Network simplex does not represent free multicast replication: after one flow reaches a branching node, sending copies to two children incurs two units of outgoing flow and cost. Therefore use it only if evaluator accounting is per copy/path, or compare its returned score against the fixed-charge candidate and retain the better valid topology. Destination-partition identity must be represented by sink copies or unambiguous flow decomposition; do not accidentally allow one destination's demand to satisfy another's. NetworkX demands must balance exactly and capacities/costs should be finite integer-scaled values when numerical robustness matters.

active_paradigms.idea: Enumerate low-cost simple alternatives with networkx.shortest_simple_paths to assign distinct partitions to genuinely different routes
active_paradigms.description: The current solution computes one shared selected tree and duplicates its exact path for every partition, which cannot exploit the stated objective of parallel paths even when several nearly equal-cost routes exist. For each destination, use networkx.shortest_simple_paths on the priced directed graph to enumerate a small prefix of increasing-cost loop-free routes, rather than considering only the single shortest route. Treat candidate paths that have different first congested edges or different bottleneck links as meaningful alternatives, and assign partitions across these candidates only when capacity or evaluator flow accounting rewards the split. Preserve shared prefixes across destinations for the same partition when those prefixes are cheaper than separate routes; this can be done by favoring candidates whose edge sets overlap a partition's already selected broadcast backbone. Because the generator orders paths by actual summed edge cost, it avoids arbitrary edge-disjoint routing that may greatly increase monetary cost. This approach is structurally different from solving one global relaxation: it directly exposes the Pareto frontier between extra parallelism and route cost that the current all-partitions-identical output hides. Limit enumeration to a small deterministic number of candidates so output is stable and runtime is bounded.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Cost-versus-parallelism trade-off: reduce overloaded repeated use of the same link while choosing the cheapest viable alternate routes and avoiding cycles.
active_paradigms.cautions: Do not blindly assign a different path to every partition, since if cost is the only scored metric and no capacity is checked, identical cheapest paths are optimal. Filter missing or nonfinite-cost edges before calling the routine, and ensure paths respect directed orientation. The function is a generator, so cap the number of yielded routes and stop once route cost is clearly dominated or sufficient aggregate throughput has been obtained. If the evaluator gives a global fixed-charge discount across all partitions, alternatives can only increase cost unless they are required for feasibility.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace the terminal-count-limited subset DP with an exact directed-Steiner mixed-integer program using scipy.optimize.milp
tried_paradigms.description: The current program is a directed Dreyfus-Wagner-style subset dynamic program: it exactly minimizes one-time edge costs for up to ten unique destinations, then falls back to a greedy shortest connection tree. This is strong because shared prefixes are charged once, matching broadcast semantics better than independent shortest paths. Its major limitations are the arbitrary ten-terminal cutoff, no explicit capacity/partition treatment, and assigning the identical complete tree path to every partition. Formulate a single MILP with binary edge activation variables x[e] and continuous per-terminal commodity variables f[t,e]. For every terminal t, impose one unit of flow from src to t, impose 0 <= f[t,e] <= x[e], and minimize sum(cost[e] * x[e]); this exactly models paying an edge once even when it serves several terminals. Add valid directed-flow conservation constraints, omit edges with missing costs, and use scipy.optimize.milp with integrality on x and sparse scipy.optimize.LinearConstraint matrices. Recover activated edges, remove cycles or unused activated arcs if any, and extract an src-to-dst path in the resulting directed subgraph before populating topology paths. This is a direct generalization of what works in the incumbent, but remains globally optimal for larger destination sets whenever the MILP solves within the evaluation time limit.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary transfer-cost score under true broadcast sharing, especially instances with more than ten destinations where the incumbent silently changes from exact optimization to a greedy heuristic.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The supplied evaluator wrapper does not reveal evaluator.py itself, so verify whether it charges unique physical edges once or charges each destination/partition traversal separately before committing to fixed-charge semantics. Do not treat an edge with cost=None as free. Use a solver time limit and accept a feasible incumbent if needed; dense per-terminal flow formulations can be large. Ensure every requested destination is reachable before extracting paths, and preserve G[u][v] edge-data dictionaries in the returned paths.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use NetworkX network_simplex as a capacity-aware min-cost-flow formulation when the scorer bills actual partition traffic rather than multicast edge activation
tried_paradigms.description: The incumbent assumes that sending data on a shared edge is paid exactly once, but it repeats the same path for all partitions and never uses the throughput field. If evaluator.py instead sums bytes carried by each path or penalizes congestion, that assumption can systematically underperform even though its Steiner tree is cheap on paper. Build one directed flow graph with each original edge capacity set from throughput and weight set to cost, give src negative demand equal to the total required partition traffic, and give each destination positive demand proportional to its requested partitions. Invoke networkx.network_simplex once to obtain the globally minimum-cost feasible capacitated flow. Decompose the resulting integral or scaled flow into src-to-destination path units and map those units to destination partitions, so partitions can use different paths rather than all copying the same tree path. For fractional throughput values, scale capacities and demands to a conservative integer granularity before calling the algorithm, then ensure the decomposition does not exceed the original capacities. This is fundamentally different from the incumbent: it intentionally prices traffic volume and balances scarce links, so it is the appropriate model if the hidden metric rewards parallel transfers or penalizes overloaded edges.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Capacity feasibility, traffic-weighted transfer cost, and completion/congestion penalties caused by sending all partition traffic through a single cheap shared prefix.
tried_paradigms.cautions: This model is not equivalent to broadcast fixed-charge cost: a shared prefix carrying traffic for multiple destinations is charged by its aggregate flow. Therefore use it only if inspection/experiments indicate the evaluator accounts for flow volume or throughput, rather than merely unique selected edges. network_simplex requires balanced integer node demands and finite numeric weights/capacities. Flow decomposition must retain destination identity; arbitrary decomposition can otherwise send a destination's partition to the wrong sink. Do not advertise flow edges as a topology path unless each listed edge is a valid directed edge in G.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use k-shortest simple directed paths to create partition-diverse low-cost route choices rather than cloning one tree path across all partitions
tried_paradigms.description: The current program deliberately finds a shared tree, but subsequently assigns exactly the same complete src-to-dst edge list to every partition. That loses the only explicit degree of freedom exposed by num_partitions and can create avoidable contention or redundant scored traversals. For each destination, use networkx.shortest_simple_paths on the directed cost graph to enumerate a small ordered candidate set of loop-free routes. Assign different partitions to distinct low-cost candidates whenever they avoid already heavily used edges, while retaining the cheapest route for partitions for which no useful alternative exists. If the evaluator deduplicates edges globally, retain paths whose prefixes coincide with an already selected backbone and diversify only after the branch point; if it prices path copies, favor alternatives with genuinely lower total path cost. Candidate enumeration also avoids the incumbent's dangerous assumption that every selected Steiner edge set will always yield a clean unique path after reconstruction. Limit the number of yielded candidates tightly, for example 4 to 16 per destination, because simple-path enumeration may grow exponentially. This idea targets the parallel-path requirement directly and is especially useful where several near-equal-cost regional routes exist.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Partition-level parallelism and load spreading while keeping each chosen route close to the minimum cost; it can improve hidden throughput or overlap terms without discarding the cheap broadcast backbone.
tried_paradigms.cautions: This technique alone does not prove global broadcast optimality, so do not replace the shared-tree strategy unconditionally on pure unique-edge-cost instances. shortest_simple_paths raises NetworkXNoPath for unreachable destinations and requires all compared edge costs to be numeric. Avoid selecting a long detour merely to be edge-disjoint unless the evaluator demonstrably rewards capacity/overlap enough to justify it. Preserve directed orientation and use original G edge metadata when storing every candidate-derived path.
